# CHOAM

**Codex for Housing, Off-Grid Architecture & Mobility** · paper v2.0

> Shelter is freedom. Homes must be open, modular, and enduring. No patent. No gatekeeper. No nation owns this.
> (Ashlynn, 2025; author's statement of values, not an empirical claim)

CHOAM is an open, copyleft standard for **government-provided** modular homes of 200 to 400 sq ft. Each unit has solar, broadband and opt-in distributed computing, and is offered as a Universal Basic Services floor. The goal is for units to be revenue-positive.

**The paper is the source of truth:** [CHOAM-Idea_Draft.md](CHOAM-Idea_Draft.md). This README summarizes it. Claim statuses are in [CLAIMS.md](CLAIMS.md). Every model-derived number below is rendered by `model/`, and `cargo test` fails if this file differs from a fresh render.

## What the numbers say

- **Solar output.** A {{kwp.ref}} kWp array in Toronto yields **{{e2.annual}} kWh/yr** (NRCan). If every kWh offset Tier-1 consumption it would be worth at most **${{e2.offset}}/yr** (OEB); the unit's consumption is not yet sourced.
- **No cash revenue.** Ontario net metering pays credits, not cash.
- **Energy-only payback.** Energy alone repays a ${{cost.low_k}}k unit in no less than **{{e4.payback}} yr** and an ${{cost.high_k}}k unit in no less than **{{e5.payback}} yr**. A {{roi.long}}-year energy-only ROI would need a unit cost of at most **${{e7.ceiling}}**.
- **Shell materials.** The partial shell materials for {{unit.sqft}} sq ft (framing, OSB, R22, drywall; Kent.ca retail, {{kent.date}}, pre-tax) come to **${{b5.material}}**, which already exceeds that ${{e7.ceiling}} ceiling. An energy-only {{roi.short}}–{{roi.long}}-year ROI is therefore impossible at any unit cost. Revenue-positive depends on avoided public costs or on a cash export tariff. Paper sections 2 and 10 explain what would have to change. The rest of the unit is not yet derived, so the ${{cost.low_k}}–{{cost.high_k}}k target is unverified.
- **Factory scale.** One factory at {{factory.large}} units/yr meets **{{s2.share}}%** of CMHC's annual need ({{cmhc.needed}} starts/yr).
- **Build speed and cost.** Factory building is 20–50% faster in the literature. On cost, McKinsey reports "more than 20 percent" savings at scale and Terner "up to 20 percent" for multifamily; neither quantifies 30%.
- **Standards.** The off-site standards are ICC/MBI 1200, 1205 and 1210, and CSA A277 is the Canadian factory-certification route. (The "ICC 1220" in earlier drafts does not exist.)

## Reproduce

```sh
cargo test                                # documents == fresh render; every other number allowlisted
cargo run -q -p choam-model               # prints the table embedded in the paper
cargo run -q -p choam-model -- --write    # re-renders the paper, README and CLAIMS from model/templates/
```
